hero.headline: US strikes Iran for second time this week during ceasefire
hero.body:
The United States launched new military strikes against Iranian targets for the second time in three days, escalating tensions as diplomatic efforts to end the three-month conflict continue. The attacks targeted attack drones and a drone ground-control station in southern Iran, according to US officials who characterized the operations as self-defense measures.

The strikes represent a significant challenge to the ceasefire agreement reached on April 7 between Washington and Tehran. Despite ongoing peace negotiations, both countries have maintained active military operations, raising questions about the viability of diplomatic solutions.

The timing of the attacks is particularly significant given recent diplomatic momentum. Just days earlier, Trump administration officials had paused Project Freedom, an initiative launched to help guide commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, to allow space for peace negotiations. Trump declared that "great progress has been made toward a complete and final agreement," suggesting the two sides were moving closer to a deal.

However, the renewed military action signals deteriorating conditions on the ground. The strikes have triggered immediate economic consequences, with oil prices climbing following news of the attacks. Brent crude jumped in response, reflecting trader concerns about supply disruptions through this critical waterway. Energy markets have remained volatile throughout the conflict, with fuel prices across the United States reaching four-year highs.

The strikes also had broader regional implications. Kuwait reported facing a missile and drone attack, though the source remained unclear. These developments underscore how the conflict continues to affect the wider Middle East despite ceasefire agreements.

The Strait of Hormuz has been a focal point throughout the three-month war. Iran had effectively choked off the waterway while the US Navy imposed a blockade on Iranian ports. Project Freedom was designed to coordinate the passage of stranded commercial vessels through these contested waters, though it was temporarily suspended to facilitate negotiations.

Iranian officials have warned against further US military intervention in the region. Ebrahim Azizi, head of the national security commission of the Iranian parliament, previously stated that American involvement in strait operations would be considered a violation of the ceasefire.

The negotiations remain described as fragile, with both nations maintaining military readiness while pursuing diplomatic channels. US officials have not provided detailed damage assessments from the latest strikes or indicated whether additional military action is planned. Iranian authorities have not yet issued formal responses to the attacks.

The conflict's economic impact continues to ripple globally. Energy bills are expected to rise for millions of consumers as the fallout from the Iran war reaches household budgets. The situation demonstrates how military escalations during ceasefire periods threaten to unravel diplomatic progress and destabilize international energy markets.

cards.headline: Oil prices jump after US strikes Iranian drones
cards.body:
Oil prices rose sharply after the United States said it shot down four Iranian attack drones. The strikes occurred despite an active ceasefire between Washington and Tehran as the two countries hold peace talks.

The military action raised immediate questions about the durability of the ceasefire agreement. The US and Iran have been engaged in negotiations aimed at ending hostilities between the two nations.

Stock markets fell in response to the news. Investors reacted to the renewed military action and uncertainty about whether the peace process would continue.

The drone strikes represent the latest escalation in a conflict that has periodically flared between the US and Iran. The two countries entered into a ceasefire agreement, but the exact terms and timeline of that agreement have not been disclosed.

Oil markets are sensitive to Middle East tensions because the region produces a significant portion of global oil supply. Any military action that could disrupt production or shipping routes typically drives prices higher.

The attack on the Iranian drones comes as peace talks between the two nations remain ongoing. The talks were intended to establish a lasting end to hostilities, but the recent military action has cast doubt on the prospects for a deal.

Market analysts noted that the combination of active peace negotiations and continued military strikes creates an unusually uncertain environment for investors. The situation makes it difficult to predict whether tensions will ease or intensify in the coming days.

Neither the US nor Iranian governments have provided details about how the drone incident will affect the ongoing peace talks.

cards.headline: Israel orders evacuations across southern Lebanon
cards.teaser: The military designated areas south of the Zahrani River as combat zones and threatened fresh strikes against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israel issued evacuation orders for large areas of southern Lebanon, designating regions south of the Zahrani River as combat zones. The military warned of fresh strikes against Hezbollah in the affected areas.

The move represents a significant escalation of Israeli military operations in Lebanon, with evacuation orders impacting multiple communities throughout the southern region.

cards.headline: Washington paper mill disaster could be deadliest industrial tragedy in state's modern history
cards.teaser: Eleven people are presumed dead after an implosion at a Longview paper mill, according to the governor.
cards.body:
Washington Governor said the Longview paper mill disaster could be the deadliest industrial tragedy in the state's modern history. Two people have died and nine others are missing and presumed dead following a tank rupture at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co on Tuesday morning.

One person who was hospitalized after the disaster succumbed to their injuries, according to the Longview fire department. Rescue and recovery operations continue at the site.

cards.headline: Kuwait reports missile and drone attack
cards.teaser: The attack comes as the ceasefire between the US and Iran faces renewed pressure.
cards.body:
Kuwait said it faced a missile and drone attack, adding to regional tensions as the ceasefire in the Iran war shows signs of strain. The source of the attack was not immediately identified.

The incident occurred as the United States conducted new strikes against Iranian targets. The timing of the Kuwait attack coincides with broader instability across the Gulf region.

cards.headline: Lebanese expect prolonged war despite US-Iran diplomacy
cards.teaser: Residents say they do not believe peace talks will end fighting between Israel and Hezbollah in the south.
cards.body:
People in Lebanon say they expect a long war to continue even if the United States and Iran reach a diplomatic agreement. Clashes between Israel and Hezbollah have intensified in southern Lebanon.

Few Lebanese believe that efforts to end the wider regional war will bring peace to their country. The fighting in the south has continued despite broader ceasefire discussions and ongoing negotiations between the US and Iran to resolve their three-month conflict.

cards.headline: Zelensky urges Trump and Congress to provide Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky asked President Trump and lawmakers to supply Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged President Trump and members of Congress to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors to help end its conflict with Russia. Zelensky said Ukraine has succeeded in defending against drone attacks but has not built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.

The Ukrainian president made the appeal directly to US leaders, seeking the advanced air defense systems as his

cards.headline: Former CIA officer arrested with $40 million in gold bars at home
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged a former CIA official with stealing hundreds of gold bars worth $40 million from the agency.
cards.body:
The FBI arrested David Rush, a former CIA official, after discovering approximately 300 gold bars worth $40 million in his home. Prosecutors say Rush stole the gold from the CIA during his tenure at the agency.

According to the criminal complaint, Rush allegedly defrauded the government by lying about his credentials. The massive cache of gold bars was found during a federal investigation. The case represents one of the largest alleged thefts from a US intelligence agency.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to multiple reports.

CNN first reported the development, stating that the probe focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury during a deposition related to her two civil lawsuits against Trump. The investigation marks a significant turn in the legal proceedings between Carroll and the president.

Carroll previously won two civil cases against Trump. In the first case, a jury found Trump liable for sexual abuse and defamation, awarding Carroll $5 million. In a second trial, a jury awarded her $83.3 million in damages for defamation after Trump repeatedly denied her allegations and attacked her credibility while he was president and after.

The allegations at the center of the cases date back to the mid-1990s, when Carroll says Trump assaulted her in a department store dressing room. Trump has denied the allegations and maintained that he never met Carroll.

The Justice Department investigation appears to center on statements Carroll made under oath during depositions in the civil proceedings. Perjury occurs when someone knowingly makes false statements while under oath in a legal proceeding. Federal perjury charges carry potential prison sentences of up to five years.

The timing of the investigation has drawn attention, coming after Trump returned to the White House and appointed new leadership at the Justice Department. Critics have raised questions about whether the investigation represents appropriate use of prosecutorial resources or potential retaliation against a Trump accuser.

The Justice Department has not publicly commented on the investigation. Representatives for Carroll also have not issued public statements in response to the reports.

The investigation adds another legal dimension to the long-running dispute between Trump and Carroll, which has already resulted in significant jury verdicts against the president in civil court.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to investigate Trump IRS settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges requested a court to reopen Trump's lawsuit against the IRS over a settlement that created a $1.776 billion fund.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges has asked a federal court to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. They argue the administration bypassed proper judicial oversight by settling the case directly with the president rather than through court proceedings.

The settlement established a $1.776 billion fund intended to compensate alleged victims of what the administration calls "lawfare and weaponization." The former judges are seeking court intervention to examine both the settlement process and the creation of this taxpayer-funded compensation program.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared husband was having stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News she was "frightened" while watching her husband's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, and she thought he might have suffered a stroke.

The debate became a pivotal moment in the presidential race, raising widespread concerns about Biden's performance. Trump went on to win the election.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra opens lead in California governor race
cards.teaser: A new poll shows Becerra pulling ahead in the crowded contest to replace Governor Newsom.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra has opened a lead in the California gubernatorial race, according to a new poll. The contest to replace Governor Newsom has drawn a packed field of Democratic candidates, with many voters still undecided.

California Democrats have shown mixed reactions to their choices in the race. The field is shifting rapidly, with multiple candidates competing for support. Observers say the election remains fluid as voters evaluate their options in the coming weeks.

cards.headline: Fair housing groups sue over federal rule change
cards.teaser: Housing advocacy organizations filed a lawsuit claiming a federal rule change stripped away protections for renters and homebuyers.
cards.body: Fair housing groups launched legal action challenging a change to federal regulations. The lawsuit argues that the rule modification removes key protections that had

cards.headline: Senators introduce bipartisan bill to reform college sports
cards.teaser: Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell unveiled legislation targeting major changes in college athletics.
cards.body:
The bill proposes a salary cap and transfer limits for college athletes. The bipartisan legislation represents an attempt to break a political logjam in Congress over how to regulate college sports amid the changing landscape of athlete compensation and mobility.

The proposed reforms include enforcement mechanisms for the salary cap and new restrictions on coach poaching. The bill emerged after Louisiana State University hired Lane Kiffin, prompting concerns about the current system. SEC leaders are discussing various scenarios as they await potential passage of the sweeping reforms, which would affect eligibility rules and transfer policies across college athletics.

cards.headline: Google employee charged over $1.2 million Polymarket insider trading
cards.teaser: The Justice Department filed criminal charges against a Google staffer who allegedly profited from insider information on a prediction market.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice charged a Google engineer with insider trading after he allegedly used nonpublic information to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The engineer made approximately $1.2 million in profits from the trades, marking the second known federal criminal case involving insider trading on such platforms.

According to the complaint, the engineer wagered over $2.7 million on bets related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign. Prediction markets allow users to bet on the outcomes of future events, from elections to corporate decisions.

cards.headline: Researchers achieve first certified perfect randomness using quantum systems
cards.teaser: Scientists at ETH Zurich created certifiably perfect random numbers using entangled quantum chips, a breakthrough for cryptography and secure communications.
cards.body:
Researchers successfully demonstrated experimental randomness amplification, producing the first certifiably perfect randomness using quantum computing systems. The achievement was published in Nature and represents a significant advance in quantum information science.

The ETH Zurich team used entangled quantum chips to generate random numbers that can be mathematically verified as perfectly random. This level of randomness has applications in cryptography, secure communications, and protecting sensitive information. Previous random number generators could not provide mathematical certainty about the quality of their randomness.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey subpoena FIFA over World Cup ticket prices
cards.teaser: Attorneys general from both states launched an investigation into FIFA's pricing for the 2026 World Cup.
cards.body:
New York and New Jersey's attorneys general have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The subpoena specifically targets matches scheduled at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

The investigation was announced by New York Attorney General Letitia James and New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport. Authorities are examining claims that fans were misled about seat locations and that FIFA's messaging about tickets contributed to inflated prices throughout the tournament.

cards.headline: FIFA faces investigation over World Cup ticket pricing
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey are investigating FIFA after fans reported being misled over ticket sales and seat locations.
cards.body:
Attorneys general from New York and New Jersey have launched an investigation into FIFA regarding 2026 World Cup ticket sales practices. The probe was triggered by reports that fans were misled about ticket availability and seating arrangements.

The investigation will require FIFA to provide explanations about how it handled ticket pricing and sales information. The focus remains on whether the soccer organization gave fans accurate details about what they would receive when purchasing World Cup tickets.

cards.headline: Spielberg Opposes AI Use in Creative Filmmaking Decisions
cards.body:
Director Steven Spielberg stated his opposition to artificial intelligence handling creative decisions in filmmaking during an appearance on the IMO podcast hosted by Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson.

Spielberg said he sees value in AI for solving medical problems but does not want the technology controlling the creative process in Hollywood. He drew a clear boundary on where he believes AI should be used in the industry.

The director explained his position by stating he does not love AI in areas where it might replace human creativity. He indicated this represents a fundamental line he will not cross in his own work.

Spielberg's comments add his voice to ongoing discussions about the role of artificial intelligence in the entertainment industry. The technology has become a topic of debate among filmmakers, writers, and actors as it becomes more sophisticated and widely available.

The director made his remarks on a podcast that features conversations with public figures. Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson co-host the show, which covers various topics with guests from different fields.

Spielberg has directed numerous films over a career spanning more than five decades. His work includes titles across multiple genres, and he remains one of the most recognized figures in American cinema.

The podcast appearance provided Spielberg a platform to address technological changes affecting the film industry. His comments reflect concerns shared by some in Hollywood about maintaining human control over artistic decisions as new tools emerge.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: The Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars during a flyby on its journey to study a metal-rich asteroid.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft captured high-resolution images of Mars as it flew past the planet. The spacecraft is traveling to study a distant metal-rich asteroid but passed close enough to Mars to photograph the planet's surface features.

The images show views of Mars' south pole and other surface features. The flyby provided a rare opportunity to photograph the red planet from a unique vantage point. Psyche used the encounter to test its imaging systems while continuing its primary mission to reach and study an asteroid in the main asteroid belt.

cards.headline: Rivian to deliver first R2 SUVs on June 9
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker set a date for initial customer deliveries of its new R2 SUV model.
cards.body:
Rivian has set June 9 as the date for first customer deliveries of the R2 SUV. CEO RJ Scaringe has called it "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date," underscoring the vehicle's significance to the company's future.

The R2 marks Rivian's expansion into a new market segment, representing a key milestone as the electric vehicle manufacturer broadens its product portfolio beyond its existing lineup.

cards.headline: Tipping expectations rise beyond US borders
cards.teaser: Tipping practices are spreading overseas as US waiting staff increasingly expect 20% or more in gratuity.
cards.body:
American tipping culture is expanding to other countries as expectations for gratuity payments rise. US restaurant staff now often express dissatisfaction when receiving less than 20% tips.

The trend has begun appearing in countries that traditionally had different payment structures for service workers. The expansion of US-style tipping practices is raising questions about whether the system is sustainable or fair outside its country of origin.

cards.headline: Triomics raises $22 million for cancer center AI tools
cards.teaser: The healthcare AI company secured Series B funding to develop oncology-specific artificial intelligence for cancer treatment centers.
cards.body:
Triomics raised $22 million in Series B funding led by Battery Ventures. The company develops artificial intelligence tools designed specifically for oncology applications at cancer centers.

The funding will support the development of specialized AI systems tailored to cancer treatment and research.

cards.headline: Australia charges woman with joining Islamic State after Syria return
cards.teaser: The woman is among several groups who spent years in a Syrian camp before returning to Australia in recent months.
cards.body:
Australian authorities have charged a woman who returned from Syria with joining Islamic State. The woman had spent years in a Syrian camp before coming back to Australia.

In recent months, several groups of women and children held in Syrian camps have returned to Australia. These returns have led to legal action against some of the returnees.

cards.headline: Appeals court allows pro-Palestinian activist Khalil to remain free pending Supreme Court appeal
cards.teaser: A federal appeals panel permitted Mahmoud Khalil to stay out of custody while he petitions the Supreme Court in his case against the Trump administration.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel ruled Tuesday that pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil can remain free while appealing his case to the Supreme Court. The three-judge panel issued the order, pausing the circuit court's previous decision.

Khalil is taking his case against the Trump administration to the nation's highest court. The ruling allows him to avoid custody while pursuing the appeal.

cards.headline: Senator Kim responds to Homeland Security chief over detention facility protest
cards.teaser: Sen. Andy Kim fired back at Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after Mullin criticized him for attending a protest at a migrant detention facility.
cards.body:
Sen. Andy Kim of New Jersey criticized Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin's comments about his attendance at a protest outside a migrant detention facility. Mullin had publicly mentioned that Kim complained about being hit by pepper ball spray during the demonstration.

Kim countered that the controversy was not a personal matter. His response underscored broader disagreements with the Trump administration over how immigration enforcement is conducted and how law enforcement treats protesters at detention facilities.

cards.headline: Georgia coach Kirby Smart suggests SEC could leave NCAA
cards.teaser: The head coach of the Georgia football program raised the possibility of the Southeastern Conference breaking away from the NCAA.
cards.body:
Georgia head coach Kirby Smart said he would support the SEC breaking away from the NCAA to play by its own rules. The comments came amid intensifying debates over college sports governance and expansion.

Smart's suggestion of SEC secession represents what some have called a nuclear option for the conference. Multiple outlets reported that SEC leaders are actively discussing contingencies as disputes over scheduling metrics and other issues continue. The potential departure would represent a fundamental shift in college sports structure, though questions remain about whether such a move would ultimately benefit or harm the conference.

cards.headline: ABC World News Tonight Wins Fourth Consecutive Emmy for Live News
cards.teaser: ABC News took eight awards at the 47th News Emmy Awards, with World News Tonight claiming the top prize for the fourth year running.
cards.body:
ABC News led all networks with eight wins at the 47th annual News Emmy Awards. ABC World News Tonight With David Muir claimed the outstanding live news program category for the fourth consecutive year.

National Geographic earned seven awards, with multiple wins for Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller. The ceremony recognized journalism excellence across numerous categories and networks.

cards.headline: Student Journalist Criticizes CBS News While Accepting Mike Wallace Scholarship
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos addressed the direction of CBS News while receiving the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School in Washington, spoke about CBS News while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards. He said the recent direction of the outlet affects the legacy of Mike Wallace.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship, which is named after the late CBS journalist. Campos is from Washington and won the award as a student journalist.

cards.headline: Film Obsession Posts Rare Second-Weekend Box Office Increase
cards.teaser: The movie Obsession saw its box office numbers rise in its second weekend, a pattern that has occurred rarely in recent years.
cards.body:
Obsession increased its box office earnings during its second weekend in theaters. The film's performance represents an uncommon pattern at the box office, where movies typically see declining numbers after their opening weekend.

The uptick generated attention on social media platform TikTok. Director Curry Barker discussed franchising possibilities for Obsession and addressed comedic elements in the film.

cards.headline: Morris Day Says He Will Not Perform at Freedom 250 Concert Despite Listing
cards.teaser: Singer Morris Day denied he will perform at a June concert on the National Mall after organizers listed him as a headliner.
cards.body:
Morris Day and the Time will not perform at the Freedom 250 concert scheduled for June 27 on the National Mall, despite organizers listing them as headliners. Day dismissed reports of his participation as rumors.

The concert is part of a 16-day patriotic celebration marking America's 250th birthday. The lineup includes Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice. Day's denial came after fans raised concerns about his advertised involvement in the event.

cards.headline: Nintendo adds Donkey Kong 64 to Switch Online next week
cards.teaser: Nintendo is expanding its Nintendo 64 game library on Switch Online with the addition of Donkey Kong 64.
cards.body:
Nintendo announced that Donkey Kong 64 will join the Nintendo Switch Online N64 library next week. The game will become available to subscribers of the online service.

Donkey Kong 64 was originally released for the Nintendo 64 console in the 1990s. The addition expands the growing collection of classic N64 titles available through the Switch Online subscription service.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Addresses Criticism Over Recent Clothing Choices
cards.teaser: Singer Olivia Rodrigo responded to online comments about her recent outfits that drew mixed reactions from internet users.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo addressed backlash over her recent clothing choices. The singer said she should not be held responsible for others sexualizing her based on what she wears.

Internet commenters posted accusations that her recent outfits both infantilized and sexualized the performer. Rodrigo weighed in on the criticism that her clothing generated online.

cards.headline: Leonora Carrington Painting From Psychiatric Confinement to Be Exhibited
cards.teaser: A work by artist Leonora Carrington created during her time in psychiatric confinement will be shown publicly for the first time.
cards.body:
A painting by Leonora Carrington created while she was confined to a psychiatric facility will be shown publicly for the first time. The surrealist artist and writer produced the work during her stay at the institution.

This exhibition marks a significant moment for the artwork, bringing attention to a period in Carrington's life when she was institutionalized. The public display of this piece offers insight into her creative output during a challenging time.

cards.headline: Kanye West Associate Seeks Court Help to Identify Anonymous Website Operator
cards.teaser: Larry Jackson filed legal action to unmask an anonymous person he says operates websites damaging his reputation.
cards.body:
Larry Jackson, who runs a label associated with Kanye West, filed a lawsuit seeking to unmask an anonymous individual operating defamatory websites. Jackson characterizes the activity as "reputational warfare" designed to damage his public standing.

The legal action asks a judge to help identify the person behind the websites Jackson says are targeting him.

cards.headline: National Trust applies fresh chalk to hillside figure
cards.teaser: Staff and volunteers will apply 17 tonnes of chalk to maintain the outline of a famous chalk hillside figure.
cards.body:
The National Trust

The National Trust is refreshing a famous chalk figure on a UK hillside by applying 17 tonnes of fresh chalk to its outline. The work aims to prevent the figure from fading due to rain and weather exposure.

Staff and volunteers are carrying out the maintenance project to preserve this well-known landmark.

cards.headline: Jimmy Kimmel Becomes Emotional Honoring Adam Carolla at Walk of Fame Ceremony
cards.teaser: Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel spoke about his friendship with comedian Adam
cards.body:
Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel grew tearful while celebrating his longtime friend and former colleague Adam Carolla at the podcaster-comedian's Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony on Wednesday. During his speech, Kimmel called Carolla his "life partner," adding a lighthearted comment about how the phrase might sound to the audience.

The emotional tribute highlighted the deep bond between the two entertainers, who have worked together throughout their careers in comedy and broadcasting.

cards.headline: Pakistan and Afghanistan continue fighting despite Chinese mediation
cards.teaser: Neither country appears ready to back down months after Pakistan declared open war on Afghanistan.
cards.body:
Pakistan and Afghanistan remain locked in conflict months after Pakistan declared open war, with neither side showing willingness to retreat. China has attempted to mediate between the two countries but has not achieved a breakthrough.

The fighting continues despite diplomatic pressure from regional powers. The conflict has persisted with no clear path to resolution as both governments maintain their positions.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over firefighting foam contamination
cards.teaser: The case centers on contamination at defense sites and represents the largest lawsuit ever brought by the Australian government.
cards.body:
Australia has launched its largest-ever legal case against US manufacturer 3M, seeking more than A$2 billion in damages over contamination from per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) used in firefighting foam. The lawsuit focuses on contamination at Australian defense bases caused by the company's products.

Attorney General Michelle Rowland announced the action against the multinational corporation over the "forever chemicals," named for their persistence in the environment and resistance to degradation.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared husband was having stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden said she was frightened by her husband's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. In an interview with CBS News, she revealed she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, and feared he might have suffered a stroke during the debate.

The comments offer insight into how the Biden family experienced one of the pivotal moments of the 2024 election campaign.

cards.headline: Australia charges woman with joining Islamic State after Syria return
cards.teaser: The woman is among several groups who spent years in a Syrian camp before returning to Australia in recent months.
cards.body:
Australian authorities have charged a woman who returned from Syria with joining Islamic State. The woman had spent years in a Syrian camp before coming back to Australia.

In recent months, several groups of women and children held in Syrian camps have returned to Australia. These returns have led to legal action against some of the returnees.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with insider trading for $1.2 million in profits
cards.teaser: The longtime employee allegedly used internal company data to place bets that violated insider trading laws.
cards.body:
A Google engineer named Michele Spagnuolo was charged with insider trading after allegedly using confidential company information to make $1.2 million on Polymarket bets. Federal prosecutors say he wagered over $2.7 million on predictions related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign.

According to the unsealed complaint, Spagnuolo had access to Google's confidential data about search trends through his position, giving him advance knowledge of outcomes that the public didn't yet know. The charges were filed in New York federal court.

hero.headline: US strikes Iran for second time in three days as negotiations continue
hero.body:
The United States conducted military strikes against targets in Iran for the second time in three days, according to reports. The attacks targeted a drone launch site near Bandar Abbas, according to multiple sources. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it responded by targeting a US airbase.

The strikes occurred during a fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran, amid ongoing negotiations to end a three-month war. President Trump has maintained maximum demands in the talks, according to reports.

The military action caused immediate market reactions. Oil prices climbed and stock markets fell following news of the strikes. The attacks come despite active diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict.

Trump denied reaching any agreement with Iran regarding the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments. The strait has been a focal point of tensions between the two nations.

The strikes represent an escalation during what was described as a ceasefire period. The US military carried out the operations targeting Iranian drone capabilities, which officials identified as an ongoing threat to American forces and interests in the region.

Iran's military confirmed the exchange, stating that Revolutionary Guard forces launched countermeasures against a US airbase in response to the American strike near Bandar Abbas. The city is home to significant Iranian naval facilities on the Persian Gulf coast.

The conflict has now entered its fourth month, with negotiations appearing stalled despite the ceasefire framework. The maximum demands maintained by the Trump administration have not been publicly detailed, but sources indicated they remain a sticking point in talks.

Financial markets reacted swiftly to the news of renewed military action. Energy traders pushed oil prices higher on concerns about potential supply disruptions from the region, which produces a significant portion of global petroleum exports. Stock indexes declined as investors assessed the geopolitical risk.

The second round of strikes in three days suggests the ceasefire remains tenuous. Both nations have military assets positioned throughout the Persian Gulf region, where previous confrontations have occurred during the extended conflict.

cards.headline: Former CIA officer arrested with $40 million in gold bars at home
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged a former CIA official with stealing hundreds of gold bars worth $40 million from the agency.
cards.body:
The FBI arrested David Rush, a former CIA official, after discovering approximately 300 gold bars worth $40 million in his home. Prosecutors say Rush stole the gold from the CIA during his tenure at the agency.

According to the criminal complaint, Rush allegedly defrauded the government by lying about his credentials. The massive cache of gold bars was found during a federal investigation. The case represents one of the largest alleged thefts from a US intelligence agency.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared husband was having stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News she was "frightened" while watching her husband's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, and she thought he might have suffered a stroke.

The debate became a pivotal moment in the presidential race, raising widespread concerns about Biden's performance. Trump went on to win the election.

cards.headline: Washington paper mill disaster could be deadliest industrial tragedy in state's modern history
cards.teaser: Eleven people are presumed dead after an implosion at a Longview paper mill, according to the governor.
cards.body:
Washington Governor said the Longview paper mill disaster could be the deadliest industrial tragedy in the state's modern history. Two people have died and nine others are missing and presumed dead following a tank rupture at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co on Tuesday morning.

One person who was hospitalized after the disaster succumbed to their injuries, according to the Longview fire department. Rescue and recovery operations continue at the site.

cards.headline: Google employee charged over $1.2 million Polymarket insider trading
cards.teaser: The Justice Department filed criminal charges against a Google staffer who allegedly profited from insider information on a prediction market.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice charged a Google engineer with insider trading after he allegedly used nonpublic information to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The engineer made approximately $1.2 million in profits from the trades, marking the second known federal criminal case involving insider trading on such platforms.

According to the complaint, the engineer wagered over $2.7 million on bets related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign. Prediction markets allow users to bet on the outcomes of future events, from elections to corporate decisions.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra opens lead in California governor race
cards.teaser: A new poll shows Becerra pulling ahead in the crowded contest to replace Governor Newsom.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra has opened a lead in the California gubernatorial race, according to a new poll. The contest to replace Governor Newsom has drawn a packed field of Democratic candidates, with many voters still undecided.

California Democrats have shown mixed reactions to their choices in the race. The field is shifting rapidly, with multiple candidates competing for support. Observers say the election remains fluid as voters evaluate their options in the coming weeks.

cards.headline: Republicans reconcile with Ken Paxton after contentious Texas primary
cards.teaser: Texas Republicans are rebuilding relationships with Paxton following a bitter Senate primary fight.
cards.body:
Texas Republicans have begun mending relationships with Ken Paxton following his contentious primary campaign for the Senate seat. Paxton secured the Republican nomination despite a bruising race that revealed party divisions.

Democrat James Talarico won his party's nomination and is now focusing his general election campaign on Paxton's past scandals. Political observers view the matchup as potentially one of Texas's most competitive Senate races in recent years.

cards.headline: Israel orders evacuation of southern Lebanon areas

hero.headline: Oil prices jump after US strikes Iranian drones
hero.body:
Oil prices rose sharply after the United States said it shot down four Iranian attack drones. The strikes occurred despite an active ceasefire between Washington and Tehran as the two countries hold peace talks.

The military action raised immediate questions about the durability of the ceasefire agreement. The US and Iran have been engaged in negotiations aimed at ending hostilities between the two nations.

Stock markets fell in response to the news. Investors reacted to the renewed military action and uncertainty about whether the peace process would continue.

The drone strikes represent the latest escalation in a conflict that has periodically flared between the US and Iran. The two countries entered into a ceasefire agreement, but the exact terms and timeline of that agreement have not been disclosed.

Oil markets are sensitive to Middle East tensions because the region produces a significant portion of global oil supply. Any military action that could disrupt production or shipping routes typically drives prices higher.

The attack on the Iranian drones comes as peace talks between the two nations remain ongoing. The talks were intended to establish a lasting end to hostilities, but the recent military action has cast doubt on the prospects for a deal.

Market analysts noted that the combination of active peace negotiations and continued military strikes creates an unusually uncertain environment for investors. The situation makes it difficult to predict whether tensions will ease or intensify in the coming days.

Neither the US nor Iranian governments have provided details about how the drone incident will affect the ongoing peace talks.

cards.headline: Pork prices in China hit 16-year low
cards.teaser: A key measure of inflation in China fell to its lowest level in 16 years, driven by weak consumer spending and oversupply.
cards.body:
Pork prices in China dropped to a 16-year low, reflecting broader economic weakness in the country. The decline stems from anemic consumer spending and an oversupply of hogs in the market.

Pork prices serve as a key measure of inflation in China, where the meat is a dietary staple. The sharp drop signals that Chinese consumers are cutting back on spending, even on essential food items.

cards.headline: China expands factory exports globally
cards.teaser: China is exporting factories across the world, prompting concern from competitors as the country's trade surplus triggers global unease.
cards.body:
Chinese companies are building factories in countries around the world, a shift that has alarmed competitors. The expansion comes as China recorded a $1.2 trillion trade surplus.

The factory exports represent a new phase in China's economic strategy. The country is poised for a record trade surplus, prompting calls for action from officials including a former Chongqing mayor. India could emerge as a winner from the global reshuffling of manufacturing.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M over chemical contamination at defense sites
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed a A$2 billion lawsuit against 3M over contamination from firefighting foam at defense sites.
cards.body:
Australia's federal government has launched legal action against 3M, seeking over A$2 billion in damages for contamination caused by per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) at defence bases. The case marks the largest legal claim ever brought by the Australian government.

PFAS, commonly known as "forever chemicals," are persistent substances that do not break down naturally and can accumulate in the environment and human body over time. The chemicals were used in firefighting foam applied at military defence sites across the country.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading on Polymarket
cards.teaser: A longtime Google employee faces charges for allegedly using internal company data to make $1.2 million on prediction market bets.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged Google engineer Michele Spagnuolo with fraud after he allegedly used confidential company information to place bets on Polymarket. According to court documents, Spagnuolo had access to Google's internal data about search trends for the 2025 Year in Search campaign and used that knowledge to inform his wagers on the prediction market platform.

Spagnuolo risked over $2.7 million on bets related to search-related trends and made approximately $1.2 million from the trades. The case is notable for involving a prediction market rather than traditional stock trading, marking a rare prosecution of this type.

cards.headline: FIFA faces investigation over World Cup ticket pricing
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey are investigating FIFA after fans reported being misled over ticket sales and seat locations.
cards.body:
Attorneys general from New York and New Jersey have launched an investigation into FIFA regarding 2026 World Cup ticket sales practices. The probe was triggered by reports that fans were misled about ticket availability and seating arrangements.

The investigation will require FIFA to provide explanations about how it handled ticket pricing and sales information. The focus remains on whether the soccer organization gave fans accurate details about what they would receive when purchasing World Cup tickets.

cards.headline: Trump Accounts app launches
cards.teaser: A mobile app for managing Trump Accounts went live, ahead of a broader rollout scheduled for July 4.
cards.body:
The White House unveiled a mobile app for Trump Accounts that became available for download. Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the app would go live, with a full program rollout planned for July 4.

The financial app allows users to manage their Trump Accounts through their mobile devices. Senator Ted Cruz described the accounts as related to Social Security privatization efforts.

cards.headline: Tipping expectations rise beyond US borders
cards.teaser: Tipping practices are spreading overseas as US waiting staff increasingly expect 20% or more in gratuity.
cards.body:
American tipping culture is expanding to other countries as expectations for gratuity payments rise. US restaurant staff now often express dissatisfaction when receiving less than 20% tips.

The trend has begun appearing in countries that traditionally had different payment structures for service workers. The expansion of US-style tipping practices is raising questions about whether the system is sustainable or fair outside its country of origin.

cards.headline: Fair housing groups sue over federal rule change
cards.teaser: Housing advocacy organizations filed a lawsuit claiming a federal rule change stripped away protections for renters and homebuyers.
cards.body: Fair housing groups launched legal action challenging a change to federal regulations. The lawsuit argues that the rule modification removes key protections that had

hero.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over contamination at defense sites
hero.body:
The Australian government filed a lawsuit against American manufacturing company 3M seeking A$2 billion in damages over contamination linked to firefighting foam.

The case centers on contamination at defense sites from chemicals known as PFAS, or per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances. These chemicals are often called forever chemicals because they persist in the environment and do not break down naturally.

The contamination is linked to firefighting foam that contained PFAS. These foams were used at military installations and defense facilities across Australia.

The A$2 billion lawsuit represents the largest case ever brought by the Australian government. The scale of the legal action reflects the extent of contamination at multiple defense sites.

PFAS chemicals have raised health and environmental concerns globally. They accumulate in soil, water, and living organisms over time. The substances have been found in groundwater near military bases where firefighting foams were used during training exercises and emergency responses.

3M manufactured firefighting foam products containing PFAS that were widely used by military and civilian firefighting operations. The company has faced similar litigation in other countries over PFAS contamination.

The Australian government's decision to pursue legal action follows years of testing and monitoring at affected defense sites. Environmental assessments documented the presence and spread of PFAS chemicals in soil and water systems surrounding military facilities.

The lawsuit seeks compensation for cleanup costs and damages related to the contamination. Remediation of PFAS contamination is expensive and technically challenging because the chemicals resist conventional treatment methods.

Australia has been investigating PFAS contamination at defense sites for several years. The government has conducted health studies and environmental monitoring in communities near affected military bases.

The case adds to growing global scrutiny of PFAS manufacturers. Regulators in multiple countries have moved to restrict or ban PFAS in firefighting foam and other products due to environmental and health concerns.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading on Polymarket bets
cards.teaser: A Google engineer faces charges after allegedly making $1.2 million through insider trading on the prediction market platform Polymarket.
cards.body:
Federal authorities charged Google engineer Michele Spagnuolo with insider trading after he allegedly used confidential company information to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. Spagnuolo risked over $2.7 million on wagers related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign and profited approximately $1.2 million from the trades.

Prosecutors allege that Spagnuolo possessed advance knowledge of search-related trends and outcomes before they became public, giving him an unfair advantage in the prediction market. The unsealed complaint details how he leveraged access to Google's confidential information to inform his betting decisions.

cards.headline: Researchers achieve first certified perfect randomness using quantum systems
cards.teaser: Scientists at ETH Zurich created certifiably perfect random numbers using entangled quantum chips, a breakthrough for cryptography and secure communications.
cards.body:
Researchers successfully demonstrated experimental randomness amplification, producing the first certifiably perfect randomness using quantum computing systems. The achievement was published in Nature and represents a significant advance in quantum information science.

The ETH Zurich team used entangled quantum chips to generate random numbers that can be mathematically verified as perfectly random. This level of randomness has applications in cryptography, secure communications, and protecting sensitive information. Previous random number generators could not provide mathematical certainty about the quality of their randomness.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: The Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars during a flyby on its journey to study a metal-rich asteroid.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft captured high-resolution images of Mars as it flew past the planet. The spacecraft is traveling to study a distant metal-rich asteroid but passed close enough to Mars to photograph the planet's surface features.

The images show views of Mars' south pole and other surface features. The flyby provided a rare opportunity to photograph the red planet from a unique vantage point. Psyche used the encounter to test its imaging systems while continuing its primary mission to reach and study an asteroid in the main asteroid belt.

cards.headline: Rivian to deliver first R2 SUVs on June 9
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker set a date for initial customer deliveries of its new R2 SUV model.
cards.body:
Rivian has set June 9 as the date for first customer deliveries of the R2 SUV. CEO RJ Scaringe has called it "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date," underscoring the vehicle's significance to the company's future.

The R2 marks Rivian's expansion into a new market segment, representing a key milestone as the electric vehicle manufacturer broadens its product portfolio beyond its existing lineup.

cards.headline: Nintendo adds Donkey Kong 64 to Switch Online next week
cards.teaser: Nintendo is expanding its Nintendo 64 game library on Switch Online with the addition of Donkey Kong 64.
cards.body:
Nintendo announced that Donkey Kong 64 will join the Nintendo Switch Online N64 library next week. The game will become available to subscribers of the online service.

Donkey Kong 64 was originally released for the Nintendo 64 console in the 1990s. The addition expands the growing collection of classic N64 titles available through the Switch Online subscription service.

cards.headline: Triomics raises $22 million for cancer center AI tools
cards.teaser: The healthcare AI company secured Series B funding to develop oncology-specific artificial intelligence for cancer treatment centers.
cards.body:
Triomics raised $22 million in Series B funding led by Battery Ventures. The company develops artificial intelligence tools designed specifically for oncology applications at cancer centers.

The funding will support the development of specialized AI systems tailored to cancer treatment and research.

cards.headline: National Trust applies fresh chalk to hillside figure
cards.teaser: Staff and volunteers will apply 17 tonnes of chalk to maintain the outline of a famous chalk hillside figure.
cards.body:
The National Trust

The National Trust is refreshing a famous chalk figure on a UK hillside by applying 17 tonnes of fresh chalk to its outline. The work aims to prevent the figure from fading due to rain and weather exposure.

Staff and volunteers are carrying out the maintenance project to preserve this well-known landmark.

hero.headline: Crystal Palace wins first European trophy with Conference League victory
hero.body:
Crystal Palace claimed their maiden European title by defeating Rayo Vallecano 1-0 in the Conference League final in Leipzig. Jean-Philippe Mateta scored the decisive goal in the second half, securing a historic achievement for the south London club.

Manager Oliver Glasner departed the club on the highest note possible, winning the trophy in what was his final match in charge. The Austrian manager performed a full-length slide on the pitch in celebration and has now won three trophies in 12 months after last year's FA Cup and Community Shield victories with Palace.

The victory grants Palace automatic qualification to next season's Europa League, a competition one level above the Conference League in UEFA's hierarchy. This represents significant European football for a team that finished 15th in the Premier League this season. Glasner suggested after the final that the club now belongs in the Europa League and should be competing at that level going forward.

The Conference League triumph comes after Palace were denied a place in the Europa League despite winning the FA Cup last year. UEFA had ruled that the club breached regulations concerning multi-club ownership, a decision that prompted this unexpected path to European football through the third-tier competition.

Mateta's goal proved particularly poignant given his recent history. The striker's move to Milan in January fell through after he failed a medical, keeping him at Palace for their European campaign. His decisive finish in the final provided redemption for those circumstances.

The achievement represents a remarkable turnaround for Palace under Glasner's leadership. The club secured their place in the top flight for a 14th consecutive season despite a demanding 12-month period that included their European campaign alongside domestic duties.

Speaking after the final, Glasner paid tribute to the players and supporters, praising their fantastic spirit throughout the campaign. He insisted he harbors no regrets about his decision to depart the club despite making history in south London.

Palace chairman Steve Parish witnessed the victory from the stands next to UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin, marking a significant moment in the club's history. Thousands of supporters who gathered at Selhurst Park to watch the final on a big screen celebrated by invading the pitch as the final whistle sounded.

The Conference League represented only the second European competition appearance for either finalist in recent memory. Rayo Vallecano, who finished eighth in Spain's top division, had previously competed in the 2000-01 UEFA Cup after qualifying through their fair play record.

With Glasner departing, Palace must now find a new manager to lead the club into next season's Europa League campaign, adding complexity to their planning after the triumph in Germany.

cards.headline: Georgia coach Kirby Smart suggests SEC could leave NCAA
cards.teaser: The head coach of the Georgia football program raised the possibility of the Southeastern Conference breaking away from the NCAA.
cards.body:
Georgia head coach Kirby Smart said he would support the SEC breaking away from the NCAA to play by its own rules. The comments came amid intensifying debates over college sports governance and expansion.

Smart's suggestion of SEC secession represents what some have called a nuclear option for the conference. Multiple outlets reported that SEC leaders are actively discussing contingencies as disputes over scheduling metrics and other issues continue. The potential departure would represent a fundamental shift in college sports structure, though questions remain about whether such a move would ultimately benefit or harm the conference.

cards.headline: Senators introduce bipartisan bill to reform college sports
cards.teaser: Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell unveiled legislation targeting major changes in college athletics.
cards.body:
The bill proposes a salary cap and transfer limits for college athletes. The bipartisan legislation represents an attempt to break a political logjam in Congress over how to regulate college sports amid the changing landscape of athlete compensation and mobility.

The proposed reforms include enforcement mechanisms for the salary cap and new restrictions on coach poaching. The bill emerged after Louisiana State University hired Lane Kiffin, prompting concerns about the current system. SEC leaders are discussing various scenarios as they await potential passage of the sweeping reforms, which would affect eligibility rules and transfer policies across college athletics.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey subpoena FIFA over World Cup ticket prices
cards.teaser: Attorneys general from both states launched an investigation into FIFA's pricing for the 2026 World Cup.
cards.body:
New York and New Jersey's attorneys general have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The subpoena specifically targets matches scheduled at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

The investigation was announced by New York Attorney General Letitia James and New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport. Authorities are examining claims that fans were misled about seat locations and that FIFA's messaging about tickets contributed to inflated prices throughout the tournament.

cards.headline: Packers running back Josh Jacobs released from custody
cards.teaser: The Green Bay Packers player was released after being arrested on domestic violence charges.
cards.body:
Josh Jacobs was released from police custody on Wednesday as the district attorney decided to hold off on filing charges while the investigation continues. The Packers running back had been arrested and faced multiple charges, including felony strangulation, stemming from allegations of domestic violence.

The DA's decision to delay charging Jacobs means he was released pending further developments in the case. The Packers have not made any public statements regarding the situation involving their player.

cards.headline: SEC leaders criticize College Football Playoff metrics explanation
cards.teaser: Conference officials challenged how the playoff committee explained its strength of schedule calculations.
cards.body:
Leaders from the Southeastern Conference issued sharp criticism of the College Football Playoff committee's explanation of its metrics. The dispute centers on how strength of schedule is calculated and weighted in determining which teams make the playoff.

The debate over scheduling metrics has intensified as conferences and teams argue over the fairness of the current system. SEC officials contend the playoff committee's methodology does not adequately account for the difficulty of their conference schedule. The disagreement comes as college football continues adjusting to expansion of the playoff format.

cards.headline: Dodgers place Kike Hernandez back on injured list
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles infielder was diagnosed with a significant oblique tear after returning from injury.
cards.body:
Kike Hernandez was placed on the injured list with an oblique tear after playing just two games following his season debut. The Dodgers activated Hernandez earlier this week, but he suffered the injury shortly after returning to action.

The team called up Alex Freeland from Triple-A to replace Hernandez on the roster. Hernandez had been dealing with a left oblique strain before making his season debut. The Dodgers also avoided placing Max Muncy on the injured list despite injury concerns.

hero.headline: Spielberg Opposes AI Use in Creative Filmmaking Decisions
hero.body:
Director Steven Spielberg stated his opposition to artificial intelligence handling creative decisions in filmmaking during an appearance on the IMO podcast hosted by Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson.

Spielberg said he sees value in AI for solving medical problems but does not want the technology controlling the creative process in Hollywood. He drew a clear boundary on where he believes AI should be used in the industry.

The director explained his position by stating he does not love AI in areas where it might replace human creativity. He indicated this represents a fundamental line he will not cross in his own work.

Spielberg's comments add his voice to ongoing discussions about the role of artificial intelligence in the entertainment industry. The technology has become a topic of debate among filmmakers, writers, and actors as it becomes more sophisticated and widely available.

The director made his remarks on a podcast that features conversations with public figures. Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson co-host the show, which covers various topics with guests from different fields.

Spielberg has directed numerous films over a career spanning more than five decades. His work includes titles across multiple genres, and he remains one of the most recognized figures in American cinema.

The podcast appearance provided Spielberg a platform to address technological changes affecting the film industry. His comments reflect concerns shared by some in Hollywood about maintaining human control over artistic decisions as new tools emerge.

cards.headline: ABC World News Tonight Wins Fourth Consecutive Emmy for Live News
cards.teaser: ABC News took eight awards at the 47th News Emmy Awards, with World News Tonight claiming the top prize for the fourth year running.
cards.body:
ABC News led all networks with eight wins at the 47th annual News Emmy Awards. ABC World News Tonight With David Muir claimed the outstanding live news program category for the fourth consecutive year.

National Geographic earned seven awards, with multiple wins for Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller. The ceremony recognized journalism excellence across numerous categories and networks.

cards.headline: Student Journalist Criticizes CBS News While Accepting Mike Wallace Scholarship
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos addressed the direction of CBS News while receiving the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School in Washington, spoke about CBS News while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards. He said the recent direction of the outlet affects the legacy of Mike Wallace.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship, which is named after the late CBS journalist. Campos is from Washington and won the award as a student journalist.

cards.headline: Film Obsession Posts Rare Second-Weekend Box Office Increase
cards.teaser: The movie Obsession saw its box office numbers rise in its second weekend, a pattern that has occurred rarely in recent years.
cards.body:
Obsession increased its box office earnings during its second weekend in theaters. The film's performance represents an uncommon pattern at the box office, where movies typically see declining numbers after their opening weekend.

The uptick generated attention on social media platform TikTok. Director Curry Barker discussed franchising possibilities for Obsession and addressed comedic elements in the film.

cards.headline: Morris Day Says He Will Not Perform at Freedom 250 Concert Despite Listing
cards.teaser: Singer Morris Day denied he will perform at a June concert on the National Mall after organizers listed him as a headliner.
cards.body:
Morris Day and the Time will not perform at the Freedom 250 concert scheduled for June 27 on the National Mall, despite organizers listing them as headliners. Day dismissed reports of his participation as rumors.

The concert is part of a 16-day patriotic celebration marking America's 250th birthday. The lineup includes Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice. Day's denial came after fans raised concerns about his advertised involvement in the event.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Addresses Criticism Over Recent Clothing Choices
cards.teaser: Singer Olivia Rodrigo responded to online comments about her recent outfits that drew mixed reactions from internet users.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo addressed backlash over her recent clothing choices. The singer said she should not be held responsible for others sexualizing her based on what she wears.

Internet commenters posted accusations that her recent outfits both infantilized and sexualized the performer. Rodrigo weighed in on the criticism that her clothing generated online.

cards.headline: Leonora Carrington Painting From Psychiatric Confinement to Be Exhibited
cards.teaser: A work by artist Leonora Carrington created during her time in psychiatric confinement will be shown publicly for the first time.
cards.body:
A painting by Leonora Carrington created while she was confined to a psychiatric facility will be shown publicly for the first time. The surrealist artist and writer produced the work during her stay at the institution.

This exhibition marks a significant moment for the artwork, bringing attention to a period in Carrington's life when she was institutionalized. The public display of this piece offers insight into her creative output during a challenging time.

cards.headline: Kanye West Associate Seeks Court Help to Identify Anonymous Website Operator
cards.teaser: Larry Jackson filed legal action to unmask an anonymous person he says operates websites damaging his reputation.
cards.body:
Larry Jackson, who runs a label associated with Kanye West, filed a lawsuit seeking to unmask an anonymous individual operating defamatory websites. Jackson characterizes the activity as "reputational warfare" designed to damage his public standing.

The legal action asks a judge to help identify the person behind the websites Jackson says are targeting him.

cards.headline: Jimmy Kimmel Becomes Emotional Honoring Adam Carolla at Walk of Fame Ceremony
cards.teaser: Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel spoke about his friendship with comedian Adam
cards.body:
Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel grew tearful while celebrating his longtime friend and former colleague Adam Carolla at the podcaster-comedian's Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony on Wednesday. During his speech, Kimmel called Carolla his "life partner," adding a lighthearted comment about how the phrase might sound to the audience.

The emotional tribute highlighted the deep bond between the two entertainers, who have worked together throughout their careers in comedy and broadcasting.

hero.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
hero.body:
The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to multiple reports.

CNN first reported the development, stating that the probe focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury during a deposition related to her two civil lawsuits against Trump. The investigation marks a significant turn in the legal proceedings between Carroll and the president.

Carroll previously won two civil cases against Trump. In the first case, a jury found Trump liable for sexual abuse and defamation, awarding Carroll $5 million. In a second trial, a jury awarded her $83.3 million in damages for defamation after Trump repeatedly denied her allegations and attacked her credibility while he was president and after.

The allegations at the center of the cases date back to the mid-1990s, when Carroll says Trump assaulted her in a department store dressing room. Trump has denied the allegations and maintained that he never met Carroll.

The Justice Department investigation appears to center on statements Carroll made under oath during depositions in the civil proceedings. Perjury occurs when someone knowingly makes false statements while under oath in a legal proceeding. Federal perjury charges carry potential prison sentences of up to five years.

The timing of the investigation has drawn attention, coming after Trump returned to the White House and appointed new leadership at the Justice Department. Critics have raised questions about whether the investigation represents appropriate use of prosecutorial resources or potential retaliation against a Trump accuser.

The Justice Department has not publicly commented on the investigation. Representatives for Carroll also have not issued public statements in response to the reports.

The investigation adds another legal dimension to the long-running dispute between Trump and Carroll, which has already resulted in significant jury verdicts against the president in civil court.

cards.headline: US strikes Iranian drone site after attack on commercial ship
cards.teaser: The US military shot down four Iranian drones and attacked a ground control station after Iran targeted a commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
The US military intercepted four Iranian attack drones and struck a ground control station in Bandar Abbas after Iranian forces launched the weapons at a commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. The strike targeted the site where a fifth drone was being prepared for launch.

This marks the second such confrontation in three days between the two nations. The incidents occur during ongoing negotiations to end the three-month conflict, though President Trump's recent Cabinet meeting remarks suggest he is maintaining maximum demands on Iran, diverging from his weekend statements indicating an agreement was near.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to investigate Trump IRS settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges requested a court to reopen Trump's lawsuit against the IRS over a settlement that created a $1.776 billion fund.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges has asked a federal court to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. They argue the administration bypassed proper judicial oversight by settling the case directly with the president rather than through court proceedings.

The settlement established a $1.776 billion fund intended to compensate alleged victims of what the administration calls "lawfare and weaponization." The former judges are seeking court intervention to examine both the settlement process and the creation of this taxpayer-funded compensation program.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans endorse Paxton after contentious Texas primary
cards.teaser: Senate Republican leaders are working to unite the party behind Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton after he defeated Sen. John Cornyn in a costly primary.
cards.body:
Senate Republican leaders are moving quickly to unite the party behind Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following a contentious primary. Senate Majority Leader John Thune spoke directly with Paxton before endorsing him, signaling an effort to redirect resources toward the general election.

The outreach reflects Republican priorities to maintain their Senate majority, with Texas emerging as a crucial battleground. Party leaders are working to consolidate support behind Paxton's candidacy after a costly primary that saw over $130 million spent between him and Sen. John Cornyn.

cards.headline: Appeals court allows pro-Palestinian activist Khalil to remain free pending Supreme Court appeal
cards.teaser: A federal appeals panel permitted Mahmoud Khalil to stay out of custody while he petitions the Supreme Court in his case against the Trump administration.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel ruled Tuesday that pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil can remain free while appealing his case to the Supreme Court. The three-judge panel issued the order, pausing the circuit court's previous decision.

Khalil is taking his case against the Trump administration to the nation's highest court. The ruling allows him to avoid custody while pursuing the appeal.

cards.headline: Senator Kim responds to Homeland Security chief over detention facility protest
cards.teaser: Sen. Andy Kim fired back at Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after Mullin criticized him for attending a protest at a migrant detention facility.
cards.body:
Sen. Andy Kim of New Jersey criticized Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin's comments about his attendance at a protest outside a migrant detention facility. Mullin had publicly mentioned that Kim complained about being hit by pepper ball spray during the demonstration.

Kim countered that the controversy was not a personal matter. His response underscored broader disagreements with the Trump administration over how immigration enforcement is conducted and how law enforcement treats protesters at detention facilities.

cards.headline: Zelensky urges Trump and Congress to provide Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky asked President Trump and lawmakers to supply Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged President Trump and members of Congress to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors to help end its conflict with Russia. Zelensky said Ukraine has succeeded in defending against drone attacks but has not built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.
